thesis: A Goblin swarm that is really a spell-count machine: bodies make the mana and set the copy count, one-target spells pointed at Zada turn each body into a card, a Treasure, a pump or a copy of itself, and one turn cashes the board into damage.

stages.label: THE RED FLOOR, AND THE BURST THAT ISN'T LAND
stages.what_it_does: Fifteen land entries and thirty-six copies (deck-facts), 29 of them red-producing lands by deck-facts' count and 32 red sources against a Karsten target of 22 by deck-audit's. deck-audit's taplands axis counts two tapped lands: Spinerock Knoll always, and Den of the Bugbear whenever you control two or more other lands. Three more enter tapped only without enough Mountains (Arena of Glory, Castle Embereth, Dwarven Mine); deck-facts' 5 counts both groups together. Sol Ring is the one rock. That part only has to hit drops. The part that decides games scales off the board, not off lands: Battle Hymn adds {R} per creature, Brightstone Ritual {R} per Goblin, and Three Tree City with Goblin named pays {2} to add one mana per Goblin, which is a net gain only past two Goblins. So once bodies exist, mana is downstream of the body count. Goblin Warchief sits here as a cost reducer: stack 004 locked Krenko at {1}{R}{R} because of it, and its haste is what let Krenko tap the turn he landed. Several lands are here for a second job, filed here because a land does one job in this model: Reliquary Tower (no maximum hand size, for a deck that draws a card per body off one {R}), War Room and Fountainport (a card each), Kher Keep and Sokenzan (bodies), Castle Embereth and Goblin Burrows (pumps), and Plaza of Heroes, whose exile mode gives a legendary creature hexproof and indestructible: the only land in the 99 that protects Zada. The Treasure-making pumps are NOT here; through Zada they turn bodies into mana and live in conversion.

evidence.note: Goblin Warchief's reduction locks Krenko at {1}{R}{R} and grants the haste for the same-turn tap
Battle Hymn and Brightstone Ritual are two of the three prior casts; the stack's four mana came from four Mountains, so it verifies their spell count, not their mana
16 of 19 sit in Mana; Battle Hymn and Brightstone Ritual cluster in Ramp, Goblin Warchief in Card Flow

stages.label: A SECOND AND THIRD BODY BY TURN THREE
stages.what_it_does: Every multiplier in this deck multiplies by creatures already on the battlefield. Zada with an empty board copies nothing; Brightstone Ritual adds one {R}; Impact Tremors fires once; Heat Shimmer copies one creature. So the first thing that has to happen is not the hub and not a ritual: it is bodies, cheaply, early. Dragon Fodder and Krenko's Command are two 1/1s for two mana; Mogg War Marshal and Goblin Instigator are two bodies off one card; Legion Warboss adds one more every turn, and Searslicer Goblin one more at each end step in which you attacked (Raid). The brief prices the declared group at 7 cards, 41.2% in an opener and 49.8% by turn three, assembling in 82.8% of games and 68.9% by turn six at mean turn 3.09 - the earliest of the three declared targets, against 4.922 for the Zada cantrip group and 6.9 for the storm payoff plus ritual. The declared group's seventh card is Skirk Prospector, which creates no tokens; it eats them, so it is held in conversion and the mismatch is filed as a proposed goldfish edit. The 3.09 is therefore the price of the group as declared, Prospector included, not of these six alone.

evidence.note: Dragon Fodder is one of the three prior casts that set Empty the Warrens' storm count at 3; the stack shows it paying storm count, not bodies
four of six in Bodies; Dragon Fodder and Krenko's Command cluster in Ramp with the other cheap sorceries
the declared component's shared roles are threat:tokens, threat:body and value:etb - properties of the cards, not evidence that they interact

stages.label: A CARD PER BODY
stages.what_it_does: Storm counts CASTS, and stack 002 established the hard half of that: copies are put on the stack without being cast, so storm count 3 becomes 8 tokens but the next spell still sees 4. Every point of count is paid one card at a time, so the hand has to refill. Seven one- and two-mana spells target only a single creature and draw: Crimson Wisps, Expedite, Accelerate, Impolite Entrance, Renegade Tactics, Might of the Meek and Ancestral Anger. Cast at Zada alone, each is copied once per other creature, so each body becomes a card (stack 001: five cards off a single {R} with four Goblins out). That is the refill, and it scales with exactly the resource the deck builds. Around it: Goblin Matron tutors a Goblin, Conspicuous Snoop casts Goblins off the top, Grenzo impulses off combat damage, Idol of Oblivion draws once a turn after a token, and Past in Flames is the rebuild, flashback on every instant and sorcery in the graveyard after a storm turn put the hand there. Daring Discovery can legally target only Zada (up to three targets), which would make it a Discover 4 per body; stack 015 on exactly that failed its checker, so it is a candidate, not a line. deck-audit reads card-advantage at 4 counted copies against a floor of 10 and lists the cantrips as possible_uncounted: the taxonomy has no pattern for a cantrip that becomes N cards.

evidence.note: Crimson Wisps targeting only Zada with four Goblins out: four copies plus the original, five cards drawn
the copies of Empty the Warrens are not cast, so a later Grapeshot sees storm count 4
six of the cantrips sit in Finishers, Ancestral Anger, Daring Discovery and Past in Flames in Ramp, Snoop and Grenzo in Card Flow, Matron in Bodies, Idol in Mana

stages.label: THE BODY PILE
stages.what_it_does: Goblins are the resource this deck converts, and they are spent four ways: counted (Zada's copy count, Brightstone Ritual, Battle Hymn, Three Tree City), copied (Heat Shimmer and its kin double whatever is here), sacrificed for mana, cards or damage, and pumped for lethal. So the pile is a stage in its own right rather than a threat count. Krenko, Mob Boss is the largest repeatable producer: stack 004 measured one activation at five tokens off a four-Goblin board, because Krenko counts himself, leaving ten Goblins. Goblin Chieftain gives the pile +1/+1 and haste, which matters because most of these bodies are made the turn they are spent; Rundvelt Hordemaster pumps it and turns Goblin deaths into chances at more Goblins. Goblin Lackey puts a Goblin from hand onto the battlefield off combat damage; Impulsive Pilferer leaves a Treasure when it dies; Fable of the Mirror-Breaker makes a Goblin Shaman, loots, and flips into Reflection of Kiki-Jiki, which copies a nonlegendary creature every turn. The ignition token makers feed this pile too; they are filed apart because they are what has to happen first. Nothing here ends a game on its own, which is the correct reading of it.
cards: Fable of the Mirror-Breaker // Reflection of Kiki-Jiki

stages.label: THE HUB AND WHAT IT COPIES
stages.what_it_does: Zada is the multiplier: an instant or sorcery that targets only her is copied once per other creature it could target, so board size is the exchange rate (stack 001). Which spell is pointed at her decides the output, which is why single-target creature spells are engine, not filler. Ancestors' Aid, Sudden Breakthrough and Reckless Ransacking each make a Treasure: through Zada, a Treasure per body, mid-turn mana that pays for the next spell. Heat Shimmer, Molten Duplication, Electroduplicate and Twinflame each make a hasty token copy of one creature: through Zada, a copy of every creature at once, so the board doubles, every copy is an ETB for the output stage, and the next cantrip draws twice as many. Stack 017 verifies it: Heat Shimmer at Zada with Mogg War Marshal and two tokens out made three hasty copies, the Marshal copy made a fourth Goblin, and the Zada token died to the legend rule - four creatures became eight. Storm-Kiln Artist mints a Treasure per cast AND per copy (stack 005), so with Zada every copy pays. Roaming Throne naming Goblin may make Zada's trigger fire twice - an open question, and the reason it is here rather than in protection. Skirk Prospector eats a Goblin for {R} (stack 004: at most ten, one shot). Skullclamp turns a 1/1 into two cards. Goblin Bombardment converts any creature, even a stolen one (stack 016), into a point at instant speed. Zada is the single point of failure: storm copies only its own spell, so no other card copies a spell pointed at one creature. engine-facts names her in six passing stacks; three concern the current 99 (001, 003, 017), since 013, 014 and 016 are about cut cards and 016 shows her not triggering. As commander, an answer to her is a tax, not a loss.

evidence.note: the copy count is the board count: four Goblin tokens, four copies

stages.label: WHERE THE BODIES LAND
stages.what_it_does: Impact Tremors, General Kreat, the Boltbringer and Purphoros, God of the Forge turn a creature entering into damage to EACH opponent - one, one and two points respectively - and the deck's best-verified multi-seat damage runs through the first: stack 002 resolves eight tokens into eight damage to each of two opponents, 32 to 24 and 28 to 20. That is a burst, not a kill: both opponents end alive. This is the stage the copy spells were added to feed: every token Heat Shimmer or Empty the Warrens makes is an entry. That is a three-card class, and no declared goldfish target measures it. Pashalik Mons prices Goblin deaths instead, one point per death at any target, which is the reach that survives a sweeper. Goblin Sharpshooter prices the same deaths as pings: it untaps whenever a creature dies, so each Goblin spent to Skirk Prospector, Goblin Bombardment or Skullclamp is one more point at any target. No stack covers it yet. Siege-Gang Commander and Broadside Bombardiers buy damage with a body at a cost, and both can point it at a player. Grapeshot is filed here rather than in wincon deliberately: stack 002 measured it at storm count 4, five instances of one damage - reach and removal, not a kill across three seats at forty life.

evidence.note: eight Impact Tremors triggers, eight damage to each opponent; the following Grapeshot sees storm count 4

stages.label: FOUR WAYS TO KEEP ZADA
stages.what_it_does: deck-audit's protection axis reads 6 copies against a 5-7 target, verdict at. Reading the six cards makes it four for the hub: Purphoros is indestructible and Roaming Throne has ward {2}, and both protect only themselves, so this model files them where they do work. The four that cover a third permanent: Swiftfoot Boots (hexproof and haste, equip {1}); Hexing Squelcher (other creatures have ward - pay 2 life, and your spells can't be countered, which protects the storm turn as well as the hub); Deflecting Swat (free while you control a commander; new targets for a spell or ability); and Untimely Malfunction, whose redirect mode does the same at instant speed and whose other modes are an artifact kill or two creatures that can't block. Plaza of Heroes is a fifth effect (hexproof and indestructible until end of turn) filed in mana. The deck's other answer to removal is structural: the rituals, Empty the Warrens, Grapeshot and Impact Tremors function with Zada in the command zone. The two redirect spells answer a single-target spell or ability, such as removal aimed at Zada, by changing its target; a sweeper has no target, so they do not answer one. That is why the pilot's interaction axis and this stage overlap.

evidence.note: Deflecting Swat and Untimely Malfunction carry protection:redirect - a property of each card, not evidence it was tested on Zada
Boots, Squelcher, Purphoros and Roaming Throne carry protection:self; reading the text, only Boots and Squelcher extend it to Zada

stages.label: THE ONE TURN, TWO WAYS
stages.what_it_does: One checker-passed ending and one checker-passed burst. Fists of Flame through the hub is the ending: stack 003 resolves copies one at a time, each drawing first, so the +1/+0-per-card locks in at +3/+4/+5/+6 on the tokens and +7 on Zada - 32 power with trample, at least 30 of it reaching an opponent at 30 life past a lone 2/2. Empty the Warrens is the wide burst: stack 002 turns storm count 3 into eight tokens and, with Impact Tremors out, eight damage to each of two opponents - who end at 24 and 20, so it sets up a kill rather than being one. The rest are team-wide pumps only because of Zada: Wild Ride (+3/+0 and haste per body), Infuriate (+3/+2) and Ticked Off (double strike) are single-target creature spells, so through the hub each one hits the whole board. Goblin Bushwhacker kicked and Great Train Heist (untap and an extra combat, or +1/+0 and first strike) are the two that work without her. The deck's former verified loop, stack 005's Haze of Rage with Storm-Kiln Artist, is gone with Haze of Rage: v1.2.0 has no verified arbitrarily-large line, and its two contained Spellbook lines both assume Krenko is the commander, which stack 004 refutes here. deck-audit reads threat-density at 1 copy against a floor of 3 because only Ticked Off carries a wincon role; this stage is the evidence that the taxonomy cannot see a pump that becomes a team pump.
